messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Writer refactor
parts:
I'm creating a new thread, so hopefully you can reply to
this.

Why not have the Writer include a method to get an ostream
to write to, as in this:

std::ostream* get_ostream();

Then you could call this method and pass it into the relevant
methods.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Writer refactor
parts:
Because there’s no guarantee that the interfaces
will implement the Writer with streams. It also
seems counter to the general callback pattern.

One option is to have the base_mcmc class
keep a stringstream internally, use that for all
of the model method calls, and then dump the
contents into the Writer callback at the end of
each transition.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Writer refactor
parts:
Allen,

Okay, everything is merged and tests passing and ready for you
to give it a shot at feature/issue-1361-writer_callback.

You should be able to reduce a bunch of code by using the
new method services, as in the now much shorter
src/stan/services/command.hpp.

I believe you’ve already implemented an interrupt callback, which
just means you’ll have to implement writer callbacks for info, errors,
algorithm output, and algorithm diagnostics. info and errors can
just point to cout/cerr (see src/stan/interface_callbacks/writer/(cout|cerr).hpp)
but if you want to guarantee absolutely silent output you can also add
switches and other fancy accouterments. I think you can have some fun
with the output and diagnostic writers — the key/value callbacks should
allow you to write useful items directly into Python memory (like the
adapted step size and metric, plus all the timings) while the std::vector
callback should allow you to stream the samples somewhere useful
as they come in.

Anyways, let me know what you think.

-Mike
